summary: Training volume over the last 4 weeks has been critically low — only 3 sessions logged (one short open-water swim, one indoor ride, and one longer open-water swim), representing a significant under-training relative to the plan's demands. Sleep is consistently poor, averaging under 6 hours most nights, and body battery readings are frequently very low (below 30), indicating chronic under-recovery. With the Half Oceanman 5km swim just 33 days away, the priority must be re-establishing consistency immediately, particularly in the water, while managing fatigue carefully.
suggestions: Your most urgent focus is swim frequency: the Half Oceanman's 5km swim is 33 days away and you've logged only 2km of swimming in 4 weeks — aim for at least 3 swim sessions per week from now through race week to rebuild feel and aerobic capacity in the water.

Your sleep is chronically insufficient (many nights under 5.5 hours) and body battery is regularly bottoming out below 20 — treat sleep as a training session and protect 7+ hours nightly; without it, training adaptations won't land and injury risk climbs sharply.

With your current low fitness base, treat Wk11 and Wk12 as a genuine re-entry block rather than a continuation of a structured plan — hit every swim and one bike/run per week consistently before worrying about hitting prescribed power and pace targets.

Your open-water swim pace on 30 Aug was ~28:47/100m at HR 161, which is very high intensity for that pace — focus on relaxed, efficient technique in pool sessions (bilateral breathing, long catch, controlled effort) to lower your HR at race pace before the Half Oceanman.

The Wk13 long run (20.5km on 20 Sept) falls only 14 days before the Half Oceanman and is too much volume at this fitness level — flag this to reduce significantly to 10–12km easy to arrive at the race with fresh legs.
